title: Varignon's theorem over the constructed reals: the midpoint quadrilateral is a parallelogram in CPoint
statement: For any four points A, B, C, D of the plane CPoint = CReal x CReal over the constructed (Bishop) reals, let P, Q, R, S be the midpoints of AB, BC, CD, DA. Then Q - P and R - S are equal as CPoint vectors, under CPoint.Equiv (the pointwise CReal.Equiv, a DEFINED Prop relation, not Eq). No non-degeneracy condition is required. This is a statement about CPoint and nothing else; it is NOT the classical Euclidean-plane Varignon theorem, which is recorded separately as F:geometry-varignon-midpoint-parallelogram and rests on a coordinatisation assumption this one does not need and does not supply.

formal.statement: theorem CPoint.varignon_vector_parallel : ((x0 : CPoint) -> ((x1 : CPoint) -> ((x2 : CPoint) -> ((x3 : CPoint) -> CPoint.Equiv (CPoint.sub (CPoint.midpoint x1 x2) (CPoint.midpoint x0 x1)) (CPoint.sub (CPoint.midpoint x2 x3) (CPoint.midpoint x3 x0))))))

evidence.supports: For any four points A, B, C, D, writing P, Q, R, S for the midpoints of AB, BC, CD, DA, the vector Q - P equals the vector R - S -- proved as `CPoint.varignon_vector_parallel` over the constructed reals (`CReal`), matching the ledger statement's vector-difference form exactly (not the weaker midpoint-of-diagonals form `CPoint.varignon_diagonals_bisect` this lane proved first).

notes:
SPLIT OUT 2026-08-22 from `F:geometry-varignon-midpoint-parallelogram`, repairing an error made the same day. That fact was 'upgraded' cas-certificate -> kernel-lean by REPLACING its `formal.statement` — smtlib2 over `Real` became lean4 over `CPoint` — and discarding its two checked witness-replay evidence rows. Those are two different propositions over two different carriers, and neither formally implies the other. Rewriting a fact's formal statement to match what was actually proved makes the ledger unfalsifiable: 'we proved X' degrades into 'we proved something we then labelled X'. So the original fact is restored intact with its CAS route and assumptions, and the kernel result is recorded here as its own fact — an addition, not a substitution. Both are true; neither overwrites the other.

SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-22, the same day as the route upgrade below. When this fact moved cas-certificate -> kernel-lean its axiom_footprint correctly emptied -- the kernel theorem rests on nothing -- and `geometry.cartesian-coordinatisation-of-the-euclidean-plane` was dropped with it. But the prose statement still claimed a result about "the Euclidean plane" while the formal statement is about `CPoint`. The identification did not vanish when the footprint emptied; it moved into the unnamed gap between prose and formal, which is strictly worse than recording it, because an explicit assumption can be audited and an unstated one cannot. It is also a STRONGER identification than the CAS route required, not a weaker one: CReal is the constructed Bishop reals, not classical R. So the prose now says what the kernel proves and names the bridge instead of deleting it. The empty axiom_footprint is unchanged and remains correct: no axiom is invoked, and the coordinatisation is not an axiom the proof uses but an interpretive step for reading the formal statement as a claim about classical Euclidean geometry.

PROOF ROUTE UPGRADED 2026-08-22, cas-certificate -> kernel-lean. The original `cas-certificate` route (a Nullstellensatz-style cofactor identity over the hypothesis ideal, degenerate in an informative way -- the generator list was EMPTY and the identity was `0 = 0`, exactly what Varignon's theorem IS in coordinates) proved the MIDPOINT-OF-DIAGONALS form first as `CPoint.varignon_diagonals_bisect` (still present in `creal_point.rs`, itself axiom-free but not what this fact states). Closing the gap to the ledger's literal vector-difference statement (`Q - P ~ R - S`) needed one missing algebraic bridge: uniqueness of the additive inverse, proved as `CReal.add_right_cancel` (seven `equiv_trans` steps from `add_zero`/`add_neg`/`add_assoc`/`add_congr`, no analysis) and then a single abstract-group rearrangement (`a+b~c+e => c-a~b-e`, `sum_swap_proof`) applied to a new single-level permutation identity `CPoint.Scalar.sum_of_midpoints_perm`. The three geometry facts this one is filed alongside (F:geometry-centroid-divides-medians, F:geometry-parallelogram-diagonals-bisect) are unaffected and remain on `cas-certificate`; nothing about their non-degeneracy conditions changes.
